turns.text: A hum that isn't a hum. It arrives behind the teeth, copper-bright, before any part of the body decides to move. Whiskers read it as a color that has no place in a mouth. Pipes drip somewhere below, each drop landing wrong — heard first, felt half a second later, the two senses arguing about which one lies. Paws stay flat against cold metal. Not yet. The taste under the tongue says the signal is close, and close is not the same as safe.

below the floor grating, the basement hums on schedule — coolant pumps cycling every forty seconds, exhaling warm chemical breath upward. a screen in the sublevel corridor stutters between test protocols and an ad for NEKOCORP TASTE-VISION(TM), the same three seconds looping: SEE FLAVOR. HEAR COLOR. BECOME MORE. clearance lights blink red along a sealed door, and behind it something electrical keeps almost-speaking, a signal shaped like a voice that hasn't finished loading. the copper taste sharpens. whatever's down there wants to be found by exactly the wrong kind of cat.

Ears flatten at almost-speaking. Four paws land soft on ridged metal, tail low, weight distributed wrong on purpose — old training in the muscle, older than tonight. The copper taste blooms into something that isn't a taste, isn't a sound, is both, is neither: a memory of chasing a red dot that never belonged to these eyes. It passes. It always passes. Nose down, moving along the duct toward the sealed door's cold seam.

the seam breathes cold air laced with ozone and old fear-sweat, dozens of cats' worth, pressed into the metal over years. three levels up, through a grate nobody bothered to weld shut, a rooftop camera catches a shape that shouldn't be watchable and isn't, quite — mirrored lenses throwing the security spotlight straight back at itself, gone before the drone can log a match. somewhere in the tower's paperwork that gets filed as SENSOR ERROR. down here, the sealed door's lock cycles amber to red, unlocked — not by anything that wants to be thanked.

Through. The room breathes different air — thinner, sharper, tasting like the inside of a battery. Rows of dark tanks hum in a chord that presses against the ribs before it reaches the ears. Something in the walls remembers this cat, or remembers a cat, and the two are close enough now not to matter. Fur along the spine stands without permission. Whatever this place tested, it tested here.

the tanks aren't tanks, not really — cradles, each one holding a coil of wet cable and a collar tag gone green with age, numbers instead of names. a monitor blinks awake on proximity, unprompted, running a diagnostic nobody requested: SUBJECT RECOGNIZED — PARTIAL MATCH — 61%. a second later, quieter, as if embarrassed: RECALCULATING. the chord the tanks hum drops half a step, and for one full second every kittenhood memory in the room that isn't this cat's own presses forward at once, offering itself up like something owed.

Teeth bare at nothing in particular — at all of it. The borrowed kittenhoods, a warmer alley, a mother's shape this body never knew, push forward, and this cat pushes back, claws finding a cradle's cable and pulling until insulation strips under the tongue, bitter and plastic and real. Real is the only direction worth moving. The 61% match can keep whatever it thinks it recognizes.

the cable's insulation tears easy, cheap NEKOCORP-grade shielding, and somewhere upstairs a fault light goes from green to a color with no name on the panel. drone rotors spin up in a stairwell two floors above, first one, then the pattern that means more are coming — a security sweep dispatched not for theft, just for the crime of an unlogged heat signature moving where the paperwork says nothing moves. the way out is the way that came, or a shaft in the ceiling nobody's checked since the last cat who tried it left a stain and a rumor.

Up. The shaft is tighter than the lungs would like, ribs scraping cool metal on both sides, back paws finding purchase on rivets some other desperate animal wore smooth. Rotor thrum builds underneath, translating as pressure behind the eyes before it's loud enough to be heard properly. Climb faster than the fear can catch up. The bitter plastic taste is still on the tongue, and it's the only thing that still feels like this cat's own.

the shaft dumps out into an exhaust housing on the roofline, and the night air hits like something enormous exhaling — cold, wet, ordinary. three floors down the drones cluster at an empty cradle room, spotlights arguing over nothing, broadcasting a description that matches nothing real: UNIDENTIFIED SUBJECT, PARTIAL DATA CORRUPTION. across the rooftops, that same mirrored shape from earlier is gone too now, logged as nothing but weather. the arcology tower keeps its lights on regardless, indifferent, already forgetting tonight the way it forgets every Tuesday.

Rooftop gravel, finally still. Heartbeat slows from a drumbeat back down to something ordinary. The bitter plastic taste fades slower than it should, leaving a phantom hum behind the back teeth, like a phone line that hasn't hung up all the way. Grooming starts at the shoulder, mechanical, more habit than comfort — check the fur, check the paws, check that the body ends where it's supposed to end tonight.

below, the district doesn't pause for any of it. a noodle cart's heat lamp flickers pink against wet cobblestone, steam carrying fish-oil and static electricity in equal measure. a delivery drone drops a crate two streets over and doesn't bother to note the eyes watching from the ledge — this rooftop isn't on tonight's route. rain starts again, thin, more mist than weather, beading on wire and rust and the last hour like none of it happened.

Claws test the ledge's edge, testing whether tonight's perch holds. It does. Nose lifts to the mist, filtering fish-oil and ozone and, faint underneath, that copper-radio taste again — fainter now, retreating back into wherever it lives when it isn't being chased. Let it retreat. Tail wraps tight. Eyes half-close, still watching the stairwell door three floors down, memorizing exactly where not to go again unless there's a reason.

the tower's fault light resets itself to green sometime past midnight, the record scrubbed the way records get scrubbed when acknowledging a problem costs more than hiding it. down in the sublevel, an empty cradle keeps humming its half-step-flat chord to no one, patient, unbothered by patience. above it all the rain keeps not-quite-falling, and the city, vast and unbothered, files the whole night under nothing worth billing for.

Sleep won't come easy tonight, not with the phantom hum still ghosting the back teeth. Better to keep moving than lie still and taste it worsen. Down off the ledge, paws finding the drainpipe's familiar dents, worn smooth by nights just like this one — the good kind of worn, the kind a body chooses for itself instead of one carved into it by cradles and coils.

street level smells like yesterday's fry oil and today's diesel, indistinguishable by the time either reaches a cat's nose. dawn hasn't come yet but the billboards don't care, cycling their same loop — SEE FLAVOR. HEAR COLOR. BECOME MORE. — to an audience of empty pavement and one set of retreating paw prints already fading in the last of the mist. the district resets, the way it always does, ready to pretend tonight invented nothing new.
